title: Hann v. Pee Dee Presbytery
disposition_detail: Held the complaint judicially out of order because Hann lacked standing (not subject to Pee Dee Presbytery's jurisdiction); because the defect could not be cured, dismissed the complaint. No merits decision. The ruling did not stay Presbytery's investigation or review of actions arising from it. Adopted 17-2; Maynard and Sartorius dissented, four were absent, and Ross recused.
first_summary: Kristin Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery was dismissed because she lacked standing before that presbytery. The SJC treated the complaint as judicially out of order and incurable, while noting Presbytery's investigation could continue. Approved 17-2, with two dissents and four absences; one recusal. No merits reasons or underlying facts appear.
summary: Kristin Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery was dismissed because the SJC held she lacked standing: she was not subject to Pee Dee Presbytery's jurisdiction, so the complaint was judicially out of order and could not be put in order. The SJC made no merits ruling and stated that the ruling did not stay Presbytery's continuing investigation or review of resulting actions. The adopted ruling was approved 17-2; Maynard and Sartorius dissented without stated reasons, four were absent, and Ross recused.
